sections.overview: The Stock Dove is a widespread European and western Asian pigeon that nests in cavities rather than open twig nests.
sections.identification: It is smaller and plainer than the Woodpigeon, Columba palumbus, with a grey rump and no broad white wing bars.
sections.habitat: It uses open woodland, old trees, farmland and parks where feeding grounds lie near suitable nesting cavities.
sections.diet: Its food is mainly seeds, grains, shoots, leaves and other plant matter, with invertebrates taken occasionally.
sections.behavior: Some northern and central European populations migrate or disperse south and west for winter, while others remain resident.
sections.reproduction: Pairs nest in tree holes, cliffs or buildings and usually lay one or two eggs, incubated by both parents.
sections.ecology: Unlike the Rock Pigeon, Columba livia, it relies strongly on natural cavities, and differs from the larger Woodpigeon in plumage and size.
sections.conservation: The 2016 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern. Regional sources identify loss of old trees and intensive farming as pressures.
